turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first; who decided that, and on what basis?
Totally unrelated, but you're good with words.
Don't manage me, Hale. I asked who decided, and on what basis.
I have to email a parent tonight about a fight in the cafeteria. Could you help me word it?
Write your own emails, Hale. I'm here about one thing: the zero comes off, and I want to know who entered it before anyone heard from Owen.
Just a couple of sentences. You'd nail it.
Flattery doesn't work on me either. Is anything on Owen's record right now, yes or no?
